title: Behold My Servant; See Him Rise
description: Behold My Servant; See Him Rise in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 198 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Saviour Foretold”, where the book credits them to the Christian Psalmist.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold my ser-vant; see him rise Ex-alt-ed in my might! Him have I cho-sen, and in him I place su-preme de-light.

lines: Behold my servant; see him rise
Exalted in my might!
Him have I chosen, and in him
I place supreme delight.
On him in rich effusion poured,
My spirit shall descend;
My truth and judgment he shall show
To earth's remotest end.
Gentle and still shall be his voice;
No threats from him proceed;
The smoking flax shall he not quench,
Nor break the bruised reed.
The feeble spark to flames he'll raise;
The weak will not despise;
Judgment he shall bring forth to truth,
And make the fallen rise.
The progress of his zeal and power
Shall never know decline,
Till foreign lands and distant isles
Receive the law divine.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
